prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1295; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the policyholder reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy declarations and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver on the policy in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and records the same general sequence of events the claimant described when reporting the loss.

Entry 4: Collected statements from two independent witnesses, both of whom describe the impact as the claimant has described it, and both confirm the claimant was seated in the driver's position.

Entry 5: Received photographs from the scene and from the body shop. The damage to the front end of the claimant's vehicle lines up with the direction and force of the reported impact.

Entry 6: Spoke with the other driver, whose account matches the claimant's on the sequence of events and the point of contact between the two vehicles.

Entry 7: Ran a prior-damage review on the vehicle using the inspection history and photos on file. No earlier damage to the affected areas is recorded, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start date.

Entry 8: Claimant's counsel submitted a medical summary reporting neck and back strain from the collision. The injury description is consistent with the mechanism and force of a head-on impact of this type.

Entry 9: Requested prior medical records. No earlier injury to the neck or back has been identified in the records returned so far.

Entry 10: Reviewed the treatment timeline. Care has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of strain, and the treating provider's notes explain the reasons for the extended course. Requested the clinical notes for further review.

Entry 11: The claimant provided a follow-up statement that added a few minor details, such as the position of a nearby sign and the timing of a brake application. The core account of the collision has remained the same across all statements.

Entry 12: Summarized the file for supervisor review. Liability, vehicle damage, driver status, and injury consistency are all supported by the available evidence. The open item is the extended treatment duration, which remains under review pending the clinical notes.
